newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli politician denies corruption allegations.
newsitem.headline: Israeli politician denies corruption allegations.

text.p: An Israeli politician at the centre of a police investigation into alleged government corruption on Wednesday denied charges he supported a candidate for attorney-general as part of a shady deal.

Aryeh Deri denied allegations he promoted the appointment of lawyer Roni Bar-On -- who resigned after one day in office last month -- in exchange for his support for the government's deal with the Palestinians for a partial troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
"That is a complete lie," Deri, leader of the Shas party, told Israel Radio in a rare interview since the allegations were first raised on Israel TV last month.
The television report said Bar-On promised Deri, on trial for the past three years on corruption charges, a plea bargain that would allow him to continue his political career.

Police questioned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about the case for more than four hours on Tuesday and said afterwards he had cooperated fully. They have already taken testimony from more than 20 people, including cabinet ministers, legislators, lawyers and journalists.

In a development that offered the Israeli media some substance in a case largely fuelled by rumour and speculation, Deri's defence lawyer announced his resignation in a letter leaked to the press on Wednesday.

In the letter quoted on Army Radio and confirmed by Deri's current defence lawyer, lawyer Dan Avi-Yitzhak appeared to confirm one of the main points under police investigation -- that Deri wanted Bar-On to be appointed attorney-general.
Avi-Yitzhak, himself a key figure in the Bar-On affair, said in the letter he was quitting Deri's defence. He accused Deri of spreading lies and slander about him.

"You have slandered me and my wife and spread lies about us and all because of my "big sin" that I dared out of pure and relevant reasons to oppose your plan to appoint Roni Bar-On as the attorney-general and I did not succumb to your will," Avi-Yitzhak wrote.
Avi-Yitzhak was one of the candidates for the office of attorney-general but was passed up in favour of Bar-On.
Asked by Israel Radio about the alleged slander, Deri said: "That is a complete lie." As for the reference in Avi-Yitzhak's letter to Deri's "plan" to appoint Bar-On, Deri said:
"Look, this is under police investigation. What the letter said, that I had a plan to appoint Bar-On, is not true."
Bar-On resigned at the end of his first day in office amid criticism he was under-qualified.
Israeli Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said on Wednesday he felt "embarrassed" by the police questioning of Netanyahu.

"I have said from the start I will not enjoy watching Israeli police interrogate the prime minister and sure enough we have reached this," Kahalani told Army Radio. "It is not a good moment for the state of Israel."
